category: Buildiq competes as a low-code, no-code application builder for Dutch public organisations, run inside Nextcloud. A citizen developer or functional administrator composes an internal app from a data model (OpenRegister schemas), pages, forms and menus (a manifest that the shared nextcloud-vue renderer, CnAppRoot and CnPageRenderer, draws at runtime), business rules, decision tables and automations, and the fleet's sibling services (documents through filinq, flows and approvals through openregister, AI agents, connections through integriq, government theming through nldesign), then versions it, promotes it, publishes it as its own Nextcloud app, syncs it to GitHub or exports it as a standalone app package. It also customises already installed fleet apps through layered screen overrides and serves page layouts and intake forms to dossiq and portaliq. The buyer compares it with the open-source low-code builders a self-hosting organisation tries first (NocoBase, Budibase, Appsmith) and with the enterprise low-code platforms Dutch government already buys (Mendix, Microsoft Power Apps). Buildiq is not the renderer the fleet's apps draw their pages with: that is @conduction/nextcloud-vue, which buildiq consumes like every other app, so a renderer defect is nextcloud-vue's and is recorded here only where it limits what a buildiq-built app can show. Written 2026-09-26 from appinfo/info.xml, 52 openspec specs, 22 manifest pages, the register fragments under lib/Settings and appinfo/routes.php at ConductionNL/buildiq@4934d09855c7; correct it here if it is wrong, because the areas and the columns follow from it.

corpus.file: app-builder/README.md (2026-03-27, the product line's market report, no per-feature ratings beyond a coarse +/- table); openregister/nocobase/ (2026-03-14, live instance, codebase and docs) and openregister/budibase/budibase.md (2026-03-21), filed under openregister although they describe the app-builder category; competitor_features for competitors 3 and 269 (Budibase), 10 (NocoBase), 92 (Appsmith), 86 and 860 (Mendix), 88 (Microsoft Power Platform). No competitor_apps row is tagged openbuild, buildiq or app-builder: the category's competitors sit under the openregister, launchpad and procest slugs.
